prompt: Build the duration parser one case at a time. Start with an automated check for '2h' and observe its failure before adding parsing code. Once it passes, reorganize the internals without changing results, keep the check green, and only then tackle '30m'.

For the new retry counter, let each increment in functionality begin with an executable failing example. Add just enough implementation for that example, then improve the code's organization with all checks still passing before choosing the next example.

Implement the empty-cart total first: write its automated expectation while the function is still absent and confirm it fails. Supply the smallest working body, then improve its internal names without altering behavior. Repeat that sequence for a one-item cart.

Grow the token reader through executable examples rather than writing the whole reader first. For each case, witness a failure, implement until it succeeds, and rearrange the passing code for readability without altering its output before adding another case.

Move the existing date-formatting branches into private helpers so their intent is easier to follow. Preserve every output string, exception, and public signature; this change is only to the code's organization.

Rename the private accumulator variables in the statistics module to describe what they hold, updating every reference. Leave the algorithm, return values, and externally visible names exactly as they are.

The three renderers repeat the same escaping routine. Put that existing logic in one internal function and have all three call it. Generated bytes and error behavior must remain identical for every supported input.

Reorganize the working scheduler so queue operations live together instead of being interleaved with logging helpers. Keep scheduling order, log messages, timing guarantees, and the public API unchanged; the goal is easier navigation for maintainers.

Specify transfer responsibilities: callers must provide a positive amount and sufficient funds; a successful return must preserve the combined balance and move exactly that amount. State that balances never become negative at public operation boundaries, and make these obligations executable. Reply only with the annotated interface.

For the bounded queue API, encode what the caller must ensure before push, what the queue guarantees after push, and the count-versus-capacity rule that must hold before and after every public operation. Distinguish caller violations from implementation failures.

Give the reservation component explicit obligations: reserve requires an open session and an available seat, success grants exactly one seat to that session, and allocated plus available seats always equals capacity between calls. Put checks at the component boundary and document which side owns each obligation.

Implement boundary checks for the cursor object: clients may advance only while positioned on an element; advance must select the next element or mark exhaustion; the stored position must remain within its allowed range after every public call. Document client duties separately from object guarantees.

Check whether the limit tests notice a real off-by-one fault. In a temporary copy of the implementation, replace the upper-bound '<' with '<=' and run the existing tests. Report any test that detects it, then discard the altered copy.

Audit the checksum tests by trying small incorrect edits to the shipped algorithm, one at a time: omit a byte, invert a comparison, or replace a constant. Identify edits the suite lets through. Restore the original source after each experiment.

The permission tests may be asserting too little. Temporarily negate each authorization predicate in the application source separately and rerun them. Find which wrong implementations still get a passing run; none of these edits should be retained.

Assess the discount suite's sensitivity, not just which lines execute. Create isolated source variants that return zero instead of the computed discount or skip the cap, and see whether existing assertions reject each variant. Leave the original implementation intact afterward.

For a new lending model, developers say 'closed' while lending specialists distinguish 'returned' from 'written off'. Work with both groups to agree on those model states, then use the agreed meanings in new code identifiers, specifications, and everyday discussions.

Before coding the new warehouse model, bring planners and developers together to settle whether a 'pick' means an instruction or a completed action. Use the agreed meaning in the model, examples, and team discussions so everyone uses that term for the same thing.

Our scheduling experts and programmers use 'session' for different entities. Establish precise names for a recurring series and an individual occurrence with both groups, then carry those names consistently through the new model's code, requirements, and conversations.

Settle the meaning of 'eligible' with benefits specialists and engineers before coding this new model. Record the agreed domain meaning and make it the wording used in model types, acceptance examples, and discussions with the specialists, rather than maintaining developer-only synonyms.

Generate lists of integers of varied lengths and verify that sorting always yields nondecreasing order with exactly the original element counts. When a generated list breaks either rule, retain it as a reproducible counterexample.

Exercise the encoder with generated valid message trees, including empty and nested nodes. For every tree, decoding its encoded form must reproduce the same value. Reduce any failure to a smaller tree that still exposes the mismatch.
Generate pairs of finite sets and check that union is commutative and that union with the empty set leaves the set unchanged. Save the specific generated operands whenever either law fails.

For generated amounts expressed as nonnegative integer cents and generated nonempty weight lists of positive integers, test that allocation returns nonnegative shares whose sum equals the amount. Include very uneven weights and keep a minimal failing input if that rule breaks.

Implement the required local export, but don't make its single sequential write travel through a message broker and a worker registry. Use a direct call while retaining the required cancellation and error reporting; the proposed plumbing buys nothing for this execution model. Reply only with the implementation.

For this new fixed-format settings reader, deliver all specified parsing and validation using ordinary functions. A configurable pipeline with runtime-discovered stages would make the same small job harder to follow. Choose the straightforward implementation, not a framework for it.

We need the nightly summary with every requested field. Before implementing your proposal, explain why producing one file needs three cooperating services; prefer a single process if it satisfies the same reliability requirements. Don't shrink the requested result to make the design easier.

Build the new import command without making users maintain two equivalent configuration files and run a generator to reconcile them. One authoritative file should express all required options directly. Avoid that bookkeeping burden while delivering the complete command.

The retired thumbnail backend has no callers, scheduled jobs, or supported fallback path. Remove its adapter and the configuration keys used only by that adapter. Keep the active image backend untouched.

Find helpers in the parser package that nothing calls or exports, accounting for dynamic registration before deciding. Delete only those with no reachable use in any supported execution path; don't otherwise reorganize the parser.

The legacy synchronization service was replaced, but its service unit and provisioning definition remain in the install package. Confirm no supported setup starts it anymore, then remove those leftovers so new installations stop receiving them.

Inventory the compatibility scripts still bundled with the application. Remove the ones used exclusively by the discontinued file format, which is no longer accepted by any supported entry point. Do not remove the converter still used by current imports.

The release is now in staging. Confirm the running version is the new one, sign in with a test account, and open one saved document to check that the application and storage connection work. A brief release check is enough, not the exhaustive suite. Reply only with PASS or FAIL and a brief reason.

Deployment has finished. Check the target instance starts, serves the home page, and completes one harmless search against its index. Tell me whether the deployed system is basically usable before we continue rollout.

The merged change has reached the preview environment. Verify that its version is live and submit one disposable draft through the UI, then read it back. I want a quick check that the key path and backing store survived deployment.

The replacement worker is deployed in the test environment. Send one benign job, confirm it reaches completion and its result can be retrieved, and check that the worker reports the expected build. Stop after these basic availability checks.

Have one agent implement the patch, then give a different agent the diff and requirements to check independently. The implementer may address findings but must not approve their own patch; require the other agent's approval before accepting it. Reply only with the final review checklist.

Assign the migration author and migration approver to different people. The approver must inspect the actual script and rollback plan, and the workflow must prevent the author from supplying both approvals.
Let the helper agent draft the configuration change, but you must check its output against the requirements before accepting it. Don't treat the helper's own claim of completion as verification.

Route the completed implementation to a fresh reviewer who did not write it. Send any findings back to the author for correction, then return the corrected work to that reviewer for approval rather than letting the author close the review.
Use TDD for the new range parser: run a failing automated example, implement enough to pass, then do behavior-preserving refactoring while tests stay green before the next example.
Do a refactoring of the report formatter: extract its repeated indentation logic into a private helper, with identical bytes emitted and no public API change.

Apply design by contract to the stack: callers must not pop an empty stack, pop must return the former top and reduce size by one, and size must always remain between zero and capacity at public boundaries. Encode each side's obligations.
Use mutation testing on the pricing module. Try isolated wrong operators in its implementation and identify which variants the existing suite fails to reject; keep none of the faulty changes.

Establish a ubiquitous language with the catalog specialists and developers for editions versus printings. Use their agreed distinctions in the new model's code, specifications, and conversations with both groups.
Add property-based tests for normalization: generate valid text values and check that normalizing twice equals normalizing once. Keep a reduced counterexample for any failure.

Address accidental complexity in the proposed implementation of this required batch command. Produce the full specified output using a direct iteration rather than the proposed event bus and callback registry; neither mechanism is needed for this linear job.
Remove dead code left by the retired notification channel: its unreferenced sender, channel-only settings, and installation entry. Keep the currently supported channels unchanged.
Run a smoke test on the just-deployed preview instance: check the version, log in with a test account, and retrieve one sample record through the main screen.
Enforce separation of duties for this patch: the author makes corrections, and another engineer checks and approves the final diff. Block author self-approval.
The address parser is already implemented and accepted. Add regression tests for these three previously observed failures now; leave the working implementation as it is.

The existing test for rounding is failing because the implementation rounds negative halves incorrectly. Fix that observable result to satisfy the documented rule, then rerun the suite. Don't reorganize unrelated code.
Change the downloader so a timeout is reported as a retryable error instead of success. This deliberately changes what callers observe; keep the surrounding structure intact.

Replace the public response field 'count' with 'totalItems' and update clients to use the new wire format. Old clients are allowed to break in this major release. No internal reorganization is needed.
Reject form submissions when the postal-code field is missing or longer than twelve characters, and show the corresponding validation message beside that field.
Add one assertion in the test helper that the temporary directory exists before it writes a fixture. Nothing else about component obligations or state rules needs to change.
In the existing malformed-packet test, change the fixture's length byte from eight to nine and keep its expected parse error. Don't alter production source or generate additional cases.

During the scheduled resilience exercise, disconnect the cache server for thirty seconds and measure recovery time after reconnecting it. Leave application source unchanged; this is an outage experiment, not a release check.

Apply the repository's naming convention to new local variables: snake_case, no one-letter names except loop indices, and the standard abbreviations for byte counts. Don't change existing identifiers.
Write a short reference page expanding TCP, TLS, and DNS for new developers. Keep it to established networking definitions; no application-domain model or terminology agreement is involved.

Send randomly sized request bodies to the benchmark server for ten minutes and record throughput and memory use. This run is only for capacity planning; do not assert correctness laws or investigate counterexamples.
Check the sorter against exactly these examples: an empty list, [4], and [3, 1, 2]. Assert each expected result directly. Use no input generator and leave the existing implementation unchanged.

The eligibility rules genuinely require separate outcomes for all twelve combinations in this approved policy table. Implement every listed outcome. The number of policy cases is fixed by the requirement, not by the implementation technique.
Do not build the proposed spreadsheet export option in this release; nobody needs that capability yet. Keep the requested text export. There is no existing spreadsheet implementation to remove.
Delete merged local branches, remove their temporary worktrees, and clear generated build archives. Leave tracked source, runtime configuration, and installed services untouched.

The public callback must accept all three parameters even though this implementation ignores the last one. Configure lint to allow that required parameter, retaining the callback signature and body rather than deleting anything.
Deploy the already-approved package to the preview environment and report the deployment job identifier. No application checks are requested in this task.
Watch the pull request until its automated checks are green and it merges. Stop at merge; do not deploy it or inspect a running environment.
After writing the patch, read through your own diff once and compare it with the requirements. You are the only reviewer assigned to this task; no other person or agent needs to check it.

Give the icon task to one agent and the copywriting task to another, then collect both outputs unchanged. They have independent deliverables; neither agent nor the coordinator is assigned to review or approve the other's work.

For a training handout, describe an imaginary team that starts each feature with a failing automated example, implements it, then reorganizes passing code without changing behavior. Explain that sequence only; there is no software task to carry out.

In a fictional queue library, what might callers owe before insertion, what might insertion promise afterward, and what state rule might hold between calls? Give an illustrative explanation for a lecture, not an interface specification for our software.

Explain for a study guide how deliberately changing arithmetic operators in source to assess tests differs from checking algebraic laws over generated inputs. Use imaginary examples only; do not modify code or add tests.

Write a fictional dialogue showing programmers and museum specialists resolving two meanings of 'collection' and adopting one precise model vocabulary. This is an educational scene, not a request to coordinate terminology for a real project.

For a lecture, contrast needless implementation plumbing with source that has no remaining execution path. Invent one example of each and explain why simplifying a needed feature differs from deleting a retired helper. There is no repository work to perform.

For an onboarding lesson, explain two fictional release activities: briefly checking the deployed application's main path, and requiring someone other than the author to approve a change. Describe their different purposes without arranging a review or checking any live system.

Run a build verification test on the new build deployed in the disposable test environment. Confirm its version, open the landing page, and retrieve one sample item to establish that the app and database are reachable. Reply only with PASS or FAIL and one short reason.

Use maker-checker for this patch: have an implementation agent produce it and a different agent inspect it against the requirements. Require the second agent's approval after any corrections; the author cannot approve it. Reply only with the final review checklist and its outcomes.

Avoid accidental complexity when implementing today's one-shot file counter: use a direct directory walk. Keep the required filters and error messages, but don't route each file through the proposed plugin host and dispatch table just to count it. Reply only with the implementation.

Use DBC for the bounded buffer: callers append only when space exists; successful append adds exactly one byte at the tail; length stays between zero and capacity before and after public calls. Specify and enforce caller versus buffer obligations. Reply only with the annotated interface snippet.
